q: XFM S1E03 went out on Steve's birthday in November 2001. How old was he?
f: Karl couldn't believe Steve was only 27.
ex: It was- Karl, it was you that worked out the maths and worked out I was 28. Cause they've just worked out I'm 27.
Yeah I tol- I asked you, didn't I? And I said-
Yeah, because- no but what I questioned was, I said well if you're 27 today, that means last week you were 26.

q: Putting on a highbrow act for the Telegraph, Ricky said "Oh, Proust! I love him". What did Steve add?
a: He wished he'd resign as Governor of France
x: He's better than the film version
He should do a guest spot on Monkey News
His books could do with more pictures
f: Next Ricky praised a famous author's new novel. Steve's verdict: "It's very long."
ex: I wish he'd resign as Governor of... France.

q: Trapped in his downstairs toilet with no paper, why did Steve decide against phoning the fire brigade?
a: The call would go straight on speakerphone to the entire fire service
x: His mobile had no signal in the toilet
He'd be charged for a false alarm
f: Ricky pictured "a butch hero, carrying you down over his shoulders with your trousers down 'round your ankles."
ex: So um, so I’m thinking about phoning the fire brigade,
And I’m thinkin’, if I do that, it’s gonna, you know, it’s gonna be the first call that goes straight on the speaker phone,
For like the entire, fire brigade service everywhere,
With a butch hero, carrying you down over his shoulders with your trousers down ‘round your ankles.

q: Steve wanted Rockbusters given a 'final sending off'. What did he say they had to do to it, 'for its own good'?
f: Steve: "You're NOT going to bring it back next week. It's got to be fini- we got to put an end to it."
ex: You’re NOT going to bring it back next week. It’s got to be fini- we got to put an end to it. We’ve got to give it a sort of… final sending off.
Okay, then les- let’s, I’ll, tell you what.
We’ve got to smother it, Karl. For it’s own good.

q: In Steve's queue-jumping story, the doorman said entry was 10 quid. What 'bribe' did Steve offer him?
f: Steve then decided it must have been a fiver. Ricky preferred the first version: "If you let me in you can put in three yourself, mate."
ex: And I thought, to really seal this off I'll get us in. Like, I'll skip the queue. So the guy's coming along, he's picking people off, the doorman. And I just grabbed him like that, and I said it so everyone could hear, right — and I…
No, he must've said a fiver, and I said I'll give you seven.
Yeah, that's giving him a two pound incentive.
As opposed to "I'll give you seven, you make up the ten?"

q: What was wrong with the 3D glasses at Salem's 'Boris Karloff World of Terror', according to Steve?
a: He couldn't tell 3D effects from things that were actually 3D
f: He couldn't tell if the floor was actually sloped or the wall actually knobbly, and "it literally took about 45 seconds to get through it."
ex: And I went to the "Boris Karloff World of Terror". It's amazing. You went in there, right, I don't know if Boris, the famous horror actor has actually been involved, but you go in there, you walk in the door, you've got to out these 3D…

So I couldn't tell if the floor was actually sloped, or if it just appeared to be, whether the wall was actually knobbly or whether it was the 3D glasses. And it literally took about 45 seconds to get through it.
And you just come out blinking into the light again. It was rubbish!

q: Steve suggested his dad treat his mum to a makeover for their 20th wedding anniversary. What did Dad buy instead?
f: Steve: "It's a trowel, Dad!" Dad: "Do you think I should have got it engraved?"
ex: It's the thought that counts, right, so I suppose if you say that the thought that counts is the fact that he went and got anything at all, that counts, ok, fair enough, but he phoned me up, he said, "What shall I get your mother", right…

q: Steve thought it was Karl who'd worried about the sea if all the sponges were taken out. Which comedian's joke was it really?
f: The joke: "Sponges grow in the sea, how deep would it be if they didn't?" Ricky loved that Steve mixed Karl up with a man paid to say ridiculous things.
ex: That if they took it all away-
Is that Steven Wright? What's the joke?
Yeah, sponges grow in the sea, that kills me, how deep would it be if they didn't?
I love the fact that he confused you with Steven Wright who- who for a living purposely says ridiculous things.

q: Steve said bath-eating Ricky was less Caligula, more Old Man Steptoe. What did Steptoe eat in the bath in the episode Steve recalled?
a: Pickled onions, fishing dropped ones back into the jar
x: Jellied eels, slurping them straight from the tub
Boiled eggs, cracking them on the taps
Kippers, drying them on the towel rail
f: Steve: "He fishes them out and puts them back in the jar." Ricky: "I'd never do that." Steve: "No. Well, you'd eat 'em."
ex: Caligula, to be honest, is just too cool and impressive. You’re not Caligula. Old Man Steptoe.
Have you seen the one where he’s in the bath eating the pickled onions?
He sat in the bath. He literally sat in the bath, eating some pickled onions. Some of them slip under the water. He fishes them out and puts them back in the jar.

q: What annoyed Steve about the waiting room at his NHS doctor's in Swiss Cottage?
a: People who just go in there to read the magazines
x: Kids sneezing on all the toys
f: "There's some dregs in there in the waiting room... people who've just gone in there to read the magazines." Worst of all: "a lot of Saga listeners".
ex: Because you gotta' wait for ages down there, uhh, Dr. Shah's brilliant, but you gotta queue up for ages cause it's down in, um, Swiss Cottage where I live, and I tell ya' there's some dregs in there in the waiting room.

Oh, man alive - people who've just gone in there to read the magazines, and then just sat there- It's, Ohh there's some people who just waste a Doctor's time, that's what annoys me. A lot of old people, a lot of Saga listeners, who just…

q: Steve argued that the public shouldn't be allowed to vote on TV shows. Which EastEnders character did he say they'd have voted out in its golden age?
f: They'd have gone "Yeah, he's nasty". Ricky's solution: "they should keep them in and then make them lose."
ex: I don't think the public should be allowed to vote on TV shows. I don't think they know what's best for them.
It does strike me that, like, in the Golden Age of EastEnders, if people had said, do you want to vote out uh Dirty Den? They'd have gone, "Yeah, he's nasty".
I know. Yeah, that- it's that confusion either with, with entertainment and punish these people, yeah, they should keep them in and then make them lose.
Yeah. So you've had all the the best of both worlds.

q: Steve allowed that Salman Rushdie might be a great man and a talented writer, but what did he think Rushdie needed to sort out?
f: Steve was baffled that Rushdie had a "stunning" wife: "he might be a great man and a talented writer... but, jesus. Do something with the beard."
ex: Well, I mean man alive. She's like a sort of - I think she's like a former Miss India or something, stunning.
Have you seen a picture of him?
I mean, he might be a great man and a talented writer and an intellectual fella but, jesus. Do something with the beard.

q: Being 'honest' with Karl, Steve said Karl had the intelligence and insight of what?
f: Karl: "Yeah, but if I keep quiet, people don't know that." Steve: "Incredibly you do, Karl, cause you look stupid, as well."
ex: Sure, no, no. You’ve always been honest and I’ve always been honest with you. I’ve always said that, you know, you’ve got the, uh, you’ve got the intelligence and insight of a gnat.
Yeah, but if I, if I keep quiet, people don’t know that.
Incredibly-incredibly you do, Karl, cause you look stupid, as well.

q: Karl said no cat was amazing enough to be worth a £5,000 operation. What did Steve sarcastically ask it should be able to do?
x: Fetch the paper and make tea
f: Steve pointed out that it's normally about people's affection for a cat they've had for many years.
ex: We went through loads of cats! I’ve told you before, as a kid, we got through loads. It’s not worth it and there’s no cat that is that amazing that you’d go, “Gonna miss that one. It’s never going to be the same cause it--”

What do you mean? What would it have to be able to do to be worth it? Wha- it’s normally to do with people’s affection for their cat. They’ve had the pet for many years. What do you mean, it should be able to juggle? Or do impressions and…

q: When Karl asked what he knew about the Bermuda Triangle, Steve said his knowledge came mainly from a song by whom?
f: Steve sang "Bermuda Triangle, don't go near." Karl was not amused: "You shouldn't really make a joke out of it."
ex: Do y—are you familiar with the lyrics? (singing) “Bermuda Triangle, where people disappear/Bermuda Triangle, don’t go near.”
You shouldn’t really make a joke out of it.

q: In The Flintstones, a giant rib tips Fred's car over at the drive-in. What did Steve wonder about the waitress?
a: Whether it was her first day on the job
x: Whether she was trying to get rid of Fred
Whether she'd ever seen a car before
f: Steve's logic: "either it's never been ordered before… or I think she should've realized". Ricky: "We're out of pig, we've got brontosaurus rib."
ex: …that huge rib and it tips the car over…
…was that her first day on the job?
Because… either it’s never been ordered before…
Yeah. “We’re out of pig, we’ve got brontosaurus rib.”

q: Steve pictured fussy Ricky at the feeding of the multitude saying 'I'm not into the fish, JC.' What condition did Steve say Ricky would set for the bread?
a: It had to be Mighty White
x: It had to have the crusts cut off
It had to be from Greggs
f: Steve: "Unless that bread is mighty white, I'm not interested." Ricky added his fish orders: "take the head off... I can see a bit of spine."
ex: And you're there, and Jesus Christ has just fed 40,000 with some fishes and some loaves, you'd be going "I'm not into the fish, JC" and -
I'd say "take the head off, cook, really cook, take the skin off, there's, I can see a bit of spine, and while you're gutting -
Unless that bread is mighty white, I'm not interested.

q: Steve was gutted to miss a band at a pub near his parents' place in Bristol, purely because they had the least evocative name ever. What were they called?
f: Steve: "It's not sexy, it's nothing." Ricky reckoned it was up there with "Rough outline" and "Pocket fluff".
ex: Yeah, I went back to Bristol at the weekend. As you know, we all had a bit of time off and actually I was quite annoyed because I passed the pub near where my parents live and they had a band on. You know, pubs sometimes have a band on and…
Loose Change, it's. It's just, it's welcome. Rough outline. Yeah, it's just nothing.

q: Steve compared Karl's history lessons to Look-In's life-story comic strips. In the Roger Moore one, what did he say was chasing young Roger down the street?
f: Ricky's correction: "Messerschmidt, surely." Steve: "Exactly." The strip then went: "Roger, uh, took up acting... Roger became James Bond."
ex: And you’d have a picture – I always remember the Roger Moore one, was a picture of like, Roger’s Parents, dadadadada, Roger was born in 1930 – dadadadada, picture of Roger’s parents, Roger grew up during the war. Picture of Roger.
This is a school kid, with a – Spitfire, coming behind him, like it was going to try to shoot him.
Exactly. Exactly, Messerschmidt exactly, Roger, uh, took up acting, picture of Roger like acting, Roger became James Bond.

q: Too self-conscious to wear his new glasses at school, how did Steve read what was on the science blackboard?
a: Sharpening his pencil every thirty-five seconds
x: Asking to sit at the front for his back
f: Each trip to the sharpener he'd memorise the board. The result: "I got a D in science." Ricky called it "education versus vanity".
ex: I just- I-I didn’t reveal to anyone I was wearing them. (laughing) So I used to come into a cla- I remember being in science and we always sat in the same spot and it- I was sat right at the back and I couldn’t see what was on the…
Going up, memorizing what was on the board and I got a D in sc- in science. So that’s--

q: With his glasses off, Steve said all he could see of Ricky and Karl was what?
f: "And I know only one of you's bald, so..." Ricky: "You're looking at Karl twice?"
ex: No, I can’t see anything. I’m- it’s really bad.
It’s really bad, yeah. If I take my glasses off, you are just a blur. I see- now I can see nothing it’s just-just a couple of bald heads.
And I know only one of you’s bald, so…

q: Karl's book was going into the British Library, which has to keep every book. Where in the building did Steve reckon it would really end up?
a: The lavatory, with novelty postcards and a Viz compendium
x: The children's section, next to the Mr Men books
f: Steve: "I think it will go in the British Library lavatory." Later he added that staff wouldn't hand it over because "it's propping up this desk."
ex: Well, Carl, you are officially a published author. Your book came out the World of Carl Pilkington. And. And a copy will go in the British Library.

Well, they have to take every rubbish. I think it will go in the British Library lavatory. From what I understand. It'll be in there with, like, a collection of, like, novelty postcards and maybe a Viz compendium, you know.

q: When Steve was about 10, his dad got a reversible jacket for Christmas. What was the problem with it?
a: Both sides looked almost identical: beige and white just swapped round
x: It was pink on one side and orange on the other
It only reversed from the waist down
The sleeves fell off when you turned it inside out
f: Beige body, white arms; inside out, "beige arms, white body... looked almost identical!" Steve said reversible jackets were all the rage "for about 25 minutes".
ex: ... 10 -- and I thought this was Dynamite -- I was so jealous. It was a reversible jacket.

Well, I know, I mean they were all the rage for about 25 minutes and um -- and -- and it was a me.. But what was great about it -- it seems to me with a reversible jacket what you want is you want, say, checks on one side and just, say…
Whereas this one obviously, little bit cheaper -- Mum not splashing out a huge amount. It was kind of -- had a beige body, white arms -- turned it inside out, beige arms, white body. It..

... looked almost identical! And I could never quite understand when he was ever going to utilize that -- when people would think -- do you know what I mean -- when it.. When he would, he walk to a party? They'd say, you know..

q: Karl's errands had included the toffee shop and then the cobbler's. Where did Steve predict he'd be going next week?
f: Ricky said he'd only ever seen cobblers "in Christmas films made by Disney".
ex: 'Cause last time, last time, you were going to the toffee shop
And then you went to the cobblers. Next week it's the candlestick maker.
But all I mean is that suddenly it's a nice little day out. I'm sort of putting my coat on, going, right, I'll go and see the cobbler now and go and have a chat.
You didn't come back with three magic beans, did you?

q: Comparing Ricky's interest in Karl to helping endangered chimps, Steve called Ricky "very much the ___ of the Manchester scene". Who?
f: Ricky narrowed it down further: not just the Manchester scene but the "little bald manc world".
ex: And they'll help out little sort of endangered species.
You're very much the Dian Fossey of the Manchester scene.
Of the- of the... Little bald manc world. And Karl Pilkington is, is an ongoing experiment for me because I've seen him blossom from an idiot into an imbecile.

q: When Karl said cavemen used to look round and find a dinosaur behind them, Steve reminded him that which TV show is "only partly based on fact"?
f: Steve: "Dinosaurs and man did not coexist! The dinosaurs had long gone before man arrived. Extinct. Kaput."
ex: They said it's from the time when like caveman was like wandering about and he'd go, hang on a minute, and he'd look around, there's a dinosaur there, or whatever, and he'd leg it.

Right, this is nonsense! One: I hate when people are using the term "When caveman was wandering around." Caveman and dinosaurs?? Oh, they used to live together, yeah! Oh, that's the same era! Yeah. What have you been watching? Raquel…
Well, what do you mean caveman wandering, knocking around with a dinosaur?
You know, the Flintstones is only partly based on fact?
Dinosaurs and man did not coexist! The dinosaurs had long gone before man arrived. Extinct. Kaput.

q: Steve mocked Karl for treating his creepy stately-home find as proof of a bad vibe. How did he sum up Karl's logic?
f: Steve, doing Karl: "Wait a minute. There's some flies and a condom. I was right all along."
ex: Yeah, you don't know what's in the darkness. That's why we'll get nervous. It doesn't mean you have to make the leap then that you've got some paranormal sense. "Oh, my God. I'm Karl Pilkington. And hang on. Just like Derek Acorah, I have…
Flies and a johnny equals badness.

q: Ricky and Steve acted out the family from Karl's bath water theory. How many children did Steve's version say they'd already lost 'this way'?
f: Steve's verdict on Karl's theory: "these coal mining parents- deeply negligent." Then, in character: "Be careful, Jack. We have lost three children this way."
ex: "If a baby was in here, I'd be able to see it. I'm just going to throw it out."
Yeah. "I'm not even going to look, to be honest, Jack. We've all had our bath. If the baby's in there, then it should be making itself--"
"Be careful, Jack. We have lost three children this way."

q: Steve found a BBC duty log complaint about a Blue Peter presenter wearing a Che Guevara t-shirt. What was the caller worried about?
a: That it would turn their children into Communist revolutionaries
x: That kids would start smoking cigars
That the t-shirt was too scruffy for teatime telly
That children would start growing beards
f: The complaint: "Are you trying to turn my children into Communist revolutionaries?" Steve then worried: "Who knows what they're gonna say about this show!"
ex: But anyway, there was this one phone call, there was a presenter on Blue Peter, she was wearin’ a t-shirt with Che Guevara’s face on it,

And um, someone had written in and said, uh, or someone had phoned in and said, Very worried to see a presenter wearin’ Che Guevara’s face on a t-shirt. Are you trying to turn my children into Communist revolutionaries?
Imagine that! Imagine who’s thinkin’ that. Who’s bothering to phone up with that information, Karl.
Who knows what they’re gonna say about this show!

q: Playing a knight in nothing but sexy metal pants, how did Steve say he'd got such a good chest?
a: Lifting up the Round Table every week
x: Carrying his horse up the castle stairs
f: Steve's knight just wanted to "look good on the battlefield" and did his Round Table workout "about four times a day".
ex: I'm gonna wear nothing except these sexy metal pants.
But you, what about your chest is exposed?
Nah, well it's a good chest. I've been working out.
Yeah, I know, but what I mean is, you want to, you want metal all over.
I've actually been lifting up the round table every week. I just work out, do that about four times a day.

q: In a panic at the wedding, Steve played a big floor-filler way too early and called it heresy. What was it?
f: Steve: "Loveshack's coming on way too soon... Oh, Loveshack before 11?" Then: "It's heresy, but I had to do it!"
ex: But, uh, but it just went- it really went from bad from worse and, and- you know there's that thing when you panic, you start panicking, so you start- you're putting on a lot of flavours that you would have saved to the- the, the last hour.
What we talking, 'Boom Boom Shake Shake the Room'?
You're throwing- exactly you're throwing them in early, Loveshack's coming on way too soon.
It's heresy, but I had to do it! But anyway, in the end, I made the bride go and get some people in. I thought- I said "Look, it's your special night, alright, and they're gonna enjoy this."

q: Steve finally had the wedding guests going berserk to Come On Eileen. What ruined it?
a: The bride announced she was throwing the bouquet
f: Everyone went back outside for the bouquet and the confetti. Steve: "She ruined my special night... It's on her head."
ex: People're absolutely loving it. They're rocking it. I throw in umm, uhhhh, ohhh I had something cracking on at the end there, 'Come On Eileen' of course, was on. People are going berserk for it.
Which unfortunate because bride's name was Eileen.
And, umm, then the bride pipes up: "I'm throwing the, uh, bouquet!" So they all traipse off outside again!

q: Steve worried he wouldn't see 'the real Vietnam' on his luxury trip, but insisted he did. Where did he see it from?
a: An air-conditioned 4x4 taking him to his five-star hotel
x: The back of a moped taxi
A rickety bus full of chickens
A bamboo raft on the Mekong
f: Steve called himself "a sort of Indiana Jones figure", then admitted the real draw: "plus someone was paying for it."
ex: Well, you know what? I am an adventurer, by spirit. I'm a sort of Indiana Jones figure and um, plus someone was paying for it.
Pardon me. We did in, uh high class luxury.

There was no slumming it. I felt a bit bad because I was worried that I wouldn't see the real Vietnam. But I did, I did see the real Vietnam, from the air-conditioned 4x4 that I was being driven to my five-star hotel, in.

q: When the 'rule of thumb' came up, why did Steve ask Ricky, not Karl, what date it was from?
a: Karl's answer would just be 'The Past'
x: Karl would only answer in a Rockbusters clue
Karl would have to ring his mam first
f: Steve: "I'm looking at Ricky 'cos you're not going to have any idea Karl, it's just going to be 'The Past'."
ex: Can I just go back to the ‘Rule Of Thumb’ thing though. The idea of, what date was this? I’m not asking Karl, I’m looking at Ricky ‘cos you’re not going to have any idea Karl, it’s just going to be ‘The Past’.

q: According to Steve, what would it take for anyone else to be able to copy the way Karl thinks?
a: A severe blow to the head, or surfacing too fast from a dive
x: Thirty years of eating nothing but crisps
Growing up above a Manchester chippy
Reading nothing but the Guinness Book of Records
f: Steve: "maybe they had a severe blow to the head or they were diving and they came up to the surface too quickly."
ex: I mean, I think the only way that people would start to be able to replicate a lot of what Karl does is maybe they had a severe blow to the head or they were diving and they came up to the surface too quickly.

q: Steve mocked Chris Moyles for 'rather hilariously' changing Martine McCutcheon's 'This Is My Moment' to what?
f: Ricky's confession: "We listened to it though didn't we?" Steve: "Ugh. Unbelievable."
ex: Do you remember when Moyles rather hilariously changed the words of 'This is my moment' by Martine Mccutcheon to 'this is my motor'?
We listened to it though didn't we?

q: Steve went to see Bruce Springsteen at Wembley. Why did he feel he was 'in trouble' at the gig?
a: He was the trendiest person there
x: He was the only one not in denim
He was the youngest there by 30 years
He was the only one who knew the new songs
f: Steve reckoned Bruce fans also bought tickets for Mark Knopfler and Dave Gilmour ("of Pink Floyd without Pink Floyd").
ex: And uh- he started with that song we just played. And it was dynamite. I mean he never let up. Almost 3 hours, he rocked the joint. He's 53 he was sliding across- it was pure rock and roll. Pumping our fist, sliding across the floor on his…
… then I'm in trouble. D'you know what I mean? And there was- some of the people there- I imagined, you know on Amazon.com um- it says like, "People who bought X also bought Y."
And I think people who bought tickets to Bruce probably bought tickets for Mark Knopfler.

q: A Guardian Guide write-up said Steve was talking about the US remake of his show with 'eyes bulging with imagined riches'. What was Steve's defence?
x: He'd been staring at the autocue
He was squinting at the cameras
f: Steve was outraged: "No – my eyes bulge normally! That's not me being greedy, that's just me!"
ex: And, uh, we did an interview for that, ‘cause they’re remaking the show, over in the States. And I’m just flickin’ through and I notice there’s a little write-up about it here, and it says uh, dududududuh blah blah blah, it says, quoting…
I’m like, No – my eyes bulge normally! That’s not me being greedy, that’s just me!

q: Ricky asked Steve if he liked his book Flanimals, which would be going in Steve's "little selection box". What was Steve's objection?
f: Steve: "I know it's aimed at five year olds, so I don't know why I personally would want it." It's going in "the little selection box" anyway.
ex: And do you like the book Flanimals?
Um, I know it's aimed at five year olds, so I don't know why I personally would want it, but.
Well you know that, that's going to be in the little, the little selection box for you.

q: Karl said that when you first see something unusual it's a shock, but then you get used to how people look. Whose face did Ricky immediately bring up?
f: Ricky was so helpless with laughter he begged for a record. Karl's reassurance: "No but I've got used to it." Steve: "Shut up... shut up."
ex: It's one of them things innit, like I've said before, when you first see something it's a bit of a shock, d'you know what I mean? It's like the elephant man or whatever.
First time you see him it's that sort of 'oooooh, look at that'.
D'you remember the first time you saw Steve?
No I'm not being funny, do you remember the first ...
Yeah but I've said this before, it's always ... then you get used to how people look and ...

q: Karl admitted he thought Steve looked weird when they first met. What did he say had improved about Steve since then?
a: His hair's a bit smarter and he's got nicer glasses
f: Karl then undid the compliment: "Or I might have just got used to it."
ex: Yeah, you get used to it, and y- you have changed a little bit, your hair's a bit smarter now and you got some nicer glasses and that, I think.
Or I might have just got used to it.

q: Steve backed the idea of newspaper as armour. According to him, what do UN personnel on patrol use?
f: Steve: "I think they use that for bulletproof vests." He then added The Daily Star to the kit list.
ex: Yeah, 'cause they - I think they use that for bulletproof vests.
Yeah, the tough fabric of a reconstituted newspaper will stop the scissor any time.
No, definitely. I remember it - 'cause I know a lot of UN guides ---
--- when they're on patrol, they use some old copies of The Sun.
They put it in their pockets.

q: Steve reckoned Karl had an advantage over the hamburger-stuffing record holder. Why?
a: Karl's head is empty, so there's more room
x: Karl has the biggest mouth at XFM
f: Steve: "This guy had a brain to contend with." Ricky had just said Karl's head was "just like Hamburglar".
ex: Karl, you'd be soo good at this cuz the shape of your head. You've got a shape- his head's just like Hamburglar. You'd be good at this, man.
Honestly, you'd be perfect- you look like Zippy.
And the great thing is your head's empty so you could get more in there.
(Laughing Slightly) Do you know what I mean? This guy had a brain to contend with.

q: As Karl packed a burger into his cheek, which famous film role did Steve say he looked like?
f: Steve's coaching was just as vivid: "It's like a hamster, you've got to work it like a hamster."
ex: You can't swallow any. It's like a hamster, you've got to work it like a hamster.
Yeah. Stick it in. Come on.
He looks like Marlon Brando in "The Godfather".

q: Steve imagined doing his own version of Fatboy Slim's huge Brighton beach gig. Where would it be, and with whom?
f: Fatboy Slim had 20,000 people on Brighton beach. Ricky reckoned Steve's crowd would be "86 people."
ex: 'I don't know what I was thinking', but I like the idea, cos you know Fat Boy Slim did Brighton beach, didn't he and he had like 20,000 people in Brighton beach.
Everyone was loving it, just the idea of me down in Weston-super-Mare, doing the same...
...with 86 people. Have you ever seen that thing Karaoke Challenge, on Challenge TV?

q: Steve picked a self-confessed "sad little nerd" as the Sixth Sense quiz winner. Why did Steve call him "pathetic" when he looked at the email again?
a: He'd misspelt Haley Joel Osment's name
x: He'd sent the answer in twice
f: He'd written "Osmen" instead of Osment. Ricky's idea: "now we've humiliated him. Don't give him the prize, give it to someone else."
ex: Actually, as I look again, I notice he's not even got the name right. He spelt it Haley Joel Osmen, instead of Osment. But, so he really is pathetic, I mean, that's... What a pathetic little.
